title: Quiz: What is a Stochastic Process?

questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes a stochastic process?
options: A single random variable describing one uncertain quantity
A collection of random variables indexed by time (or another parameter)
A deterministic function with added noise at one time point
A probability distribution over a finite set of outcomes
questions.explanation: A stochastic process is an indexed collection {X(t) : t ∈ T} of random variables — it tracks how randomness evolves across an entire index set, not just at one instant.

questions.text: The state space S of a stochastic process must always be a finite set.
questions.explanation: The state space S can be finite (e.g., {Healthy, Sick, Dead}), countably infinite (e.g., {0, 1, 2, ...}), or uncountably infinite (e.g., ℝ or [0, ∞)). There is no requirement for S to be finite.

questions.text: A hospital records the number of patients in the emergency room at the end of each hour. What type of stochastic process is this?
questions.explanation: Observations happen at discrete hourly intervals (T = {0, 1, 2, ...} hours), and the patient count is a non-negative integer (S = {0, 1, 2, ...}). Both index set and state space are discrete.

questions.text: A patient's clinical status (Healthy / Infected / Recovered) can change at any moment in real time. What type of stochastic process describes this?
options: Discrete time, discrete state — because there are only 3 states
Continuous time, discrete state — because states are discrete but transitions happen in continuous time
Continuous time, continuous state — because time is continuous
Discrete time, continuous state — because health is a continuous concept
questions.explanation: Time is continuous (T = [0, ∞)) because the patient can change state at any instant. The state space S = {Healthy, Infected, Recovered} is discrete (three distinct labels). This makes it continuous time, discrete state — the type that includes Markov chains and birth-death processes.

questions.text: In the notation {X(t) : t ∈ T}, a single observed trajectory of the process (e.g., one run of a simulation) is called:
questions.explanation: A sample path (also called a realization or trajectory) is one specific sequence of values t ↦ X(t, ω) that results when the random process plays out for a particular ω ∈ Ω. Running the same simulation multiple times produces different sample paths from the same process.

questions.text: A stochastic process with discrete time and continuous state can be used to model daily recorded body temperature, where the temperature is a real number.
questions.explanation: Daily observations give a discrete index set T = {1, 2, 3, ...}. Body temperature is a real-valued continuous quantity, so S ⊆ ℝ. This is exactly the discrete-time, continuous-state type.
